newsitem.title: USA: Poll shows drop in support for Gore as president.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows drop in support for Gore as president.

text.p: Nearly half of the respondents in a new poll released Friday said they did not believe Vice President Al Gore would make a good president if he were elected in 2000.

The Time Magazine/CNN poll said when participants were asked to choose exclusively from Democratic contenders who might run for president in the next election, 41 percent said they would vote for Gore.

However, when asked if they felt Al Gore would make a good president to succeed Clinton, 49 percent said they did not think he would. A similar poll in October showed 39 percent felt Gore would not make a good president.
Running a distant second to Gore in the Democratic field was the Rev. Jesse Jackson, who got 15 percent of the vote, and former Sen. Bill Bradley came in third with eight percent.
Gore faced a storm of ethics questions and a possible dip in popularity this month after reports he had solicited campaign funds by telephone from his White House office.

According to the poll, which surveyed 1,018 adult Americans by phone, 60 percent thought Gore's phone calls from the White House seeking contributions were inappropriate, while 44 percent said his actions were unethical.
The poll reported a 3.1 percent margin of error.
